title: Immature Teratoma, Embryonal Carcinoma & BEP Chemotherapy: Grading, Serum Tumor Markers and Fertility Preservation
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 18
DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology 11th Edition Ch 85
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Ovarian Cancer/Malignant Germ Cell (Version 1.2024)

steps.say: Immature teratoma is a malignant germ cell tumor containing tissues derived from all three embryonic germ layers, graded pathologically by the quantity of immature neuroectodermal elements.
steps.tx: Histological **Thurlbeck and Scully grading** stratifies immature teratoma based on the quantity of **immature neuroepithelium** per slide: **Grade 1 <=1 LPF**, Grade 2 spans 1 to 3 low-power fields, and **Grade 3 >=4 LPFs** (or >3.75 mm aggregate area), directly dictating biological aggressiveness and adjuvant chemotherapy requirements.

vis.alt: Ultrasound image displaying cystic-solid adnexal mass with characteristic internal acoustic shadowing.

steps.say: Stage one grade one immature teratoma exhibits an exceptionally favorable prognosis and does not require adjuvant cytotoxic chemotherapy following surgical resection.
steps.tx: In patients with **Stage IA Grade 1** immature teratoma, surgical resection alone achieves long-term disease-free survival exceeding 95%, allowing safe **omission of adjuvant chemo**. Conversely, **Grade 2-3 or Stage IC-IV** disease warrants immediate systemic combination chemotherapy to prevent aggressive intra-abdominal recurrence.

left.title: Stage IA Grade 1 (Favorable)
points: Encapsulated tumor strictly confined to one ovary
Immature neuroepithelium limited to <= 1 low-power field
Surgery alone curative; no adjuvant chemotherapy required

right.title: Grade 2/3 or Stage IC-IV (High Risk)
points: Extensive immature neuroectoderm or capsular rupture/ascites
High propensity for rapid peritoneal dissemination

steps.say: Embryonal carcinoma of the ovary is a highly malignant, primitive germ cell neoplasm characterized by distinctive dual biomarker elevation.
steps.tx: **Embryonal carcinoma** produces both **elevated AFP and beta-hCG**, while **yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor)** secretes solely AFP and pathognomonically displays **Schiller-Duval bodies** (central blood vessel surrounded by primitive germ cells within a cystic space). Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

steps.say: The BEP regimen is the worldwide gold standard cytotoxic chemotherapy protocol for malignant ovarian germ cell neoplasms.
steps.tx: The definitive **BEP regimen** comprises **bleomycin etoposide cisplatin**. Standard administration consists of etoposide 100 mg/m2 daily for 5 days, cisplatin 20 mg/m2 daily for 5 days, and weekly bleomycin 30 units (maximum cumulative dose <= 400 units to prevent pulmonary toxicity), delivered every 21 days.

steps.say: The number of chemotherapy cycles in malignant germ cell tumors is tailored according to postoperative surgical residual and risk stratification.
steps.tx: Patients with completely resected early-stage disease receive **3 cycles BEP adjuvant**, whereas bulky residual disease or advanced metastatic presentation mandates **4 cycles advanced BEP**, achieving an overall cure rate of **90-95% cure rate** across prospective international GOG trials. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Completely resected disease: administer 3 cycles of BEP every 21 days
Bulky macroscopic residual or Stage IV disease: administer 4 cycles of BEP
Attain durable long-term radiographic and biochemical cure in >90% of cases

steps.say: Because malignant ovarian germ cell tumors occur predominantly in children and young women, surgical treatment must prioritize reproductive conservation.
steps.tx: Primary surgical management consists of **fertility-sparing USO** (unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy) with comprehensive surgical staging. Contralateral ovarian wedge resection carries an absolute **contraindication to routine bivalving**, as occult bilateral involvement is rare (<5% in non-dysgerminoma) and surgical trauma risks mechanical infertility. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Fertility-Sparing Principles
points: Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with intact capsule preservation
Thorough peritoneal washings and infracolic omentectomy
Careful visual inspection and palpation of contralateral ovary

right.title: Prohibited Surgical Practices
points: Routine bivalving or wedge biopsy of normal contralateral ovary
Unnecessary bilateral oophorectomy or hysterectomy in young patients
Blind morcellation or cyst rupture inside peritoneal cavity

steps.say: During or following chemotherapy for immature teratoma, enlarging peritoneal masses may develop that represent fully benign differentiated teratomatous implants.
steps.tx: The **growing teratoma syndrome** presents as paradoxical enlargement of metastatic masses during or after systemic chemotherapy despite **normalizing tumor markers** (AFP and hCG). Histopathological biopsy demonstrates **mature teratoma histology** entirely devoid of malignant immature elements, which is managed definitively with surgical resection.

nodes.label: Patient with immature teratoma completes cytotoxic BEP chemotherapy
Serial serum AFP and beta-hCG levels drop to completely normal ranges
Surveillance CT scans show paradoxical enlarging intra-abdominal masses
Perform surgical resection: confirm 100% benign mature teratoma (GTS)

steps.say: Bleomycin-induced pulmonary toxicity is a potentially fatal complication that requires strict lifetime precautions regarding oxygen administration.
steps.tx: Bleomycin causes oxidative alveolar damage leading to **bleomycin pulmonary toxicity** with severe lung fibrosis. Patients require baseline **DLCO monitoring** before each cycle (withholding drug if DLCO drops >20%) and lifelong avoidance of **hyperoxia avoidance (FiO2 <30%)** during future surgical general anaesthesia.
